transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 57m
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Nguyen (Redwood Solutions), Priya Ramesh (AegisCloud Lead ML), Marco Silva (Aegis SRE), Diane Holt (Aegis PM)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): Quick discovery to quantify workload characteristics — baseline QPS, typical concurrency, tail burst factor and token sizes. Capture success criteria for pilot: P99 latency targets, cost-per-1k-tokens ceiling, and acceptability thresholds for hallucination/quality baselines.

Topics covered: traffic surface, token-drift over time, benchmark plan, infra options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), security gating.

00:00:10 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this tightly focused, I think we have about 55 minutes. quick intros?
00:00:18 Priya: sure, i'm priya, lead ml at aegiscloud, we run the customer support assistant and a couple of internal analytics microservices, trying to, you know, see if redwood can economically run our gen calls at scale.
00:00:28 Marco: marco, SRE. most interested in tail noise and peaking, we have some egress rules and…we also need to understand private connectivity.
00:00:34 Diane: diane, product, i'll be tracking success criteria and timelines.
00:00:39 Alex: great. samir, quick one-sentence on what we'll drill into.
00:00:43 Samir: yeah, we'll try to capture the traffic distribution — qps baseline, burst factors, token input/output distributions — and then map to a benchmark plan that tests P95/P99 latency and cost at typical and peak patterns. also talk infra choices if you need vpc/on-prem.

00:01:05 Priya: high level context: our average QPS currently is around 18 during business hours, lower at nights, but we have these daily spikes from batch jobs — roughly a 6x burst for maybe 5-7 minutes. also we have multiple request types, quick intent classification ~50 tokens in/out, and full-conversation generation where outputs average 600 tokens and can go up to 2.5k.
00:01:30 Samir: ok that's useful, when you say 6x burst, is that concurrent or just qps?
00:01:35 Priya: it's qps, so concurrency scales up accordingly, our concurrency at baseline maybe 40, during peaks it hits ~260.
00:01:42 Alex: and do you have a token distribution histogram or at least percentiles?
00:01:46 Priya: we do, i'll extract a CSV. rough numbers — 50th percentile prompt+response ~180 tokens, 75th ~420, 90th ~900, 99th > 1.8k. small endpoint of classification is heavy on qps but light on tokens.
00:02:00 Jules: quick clarifying q: when you say "prompt+response" are you including few-shot context? some of your flows have dynamic contexts that add 200-400 tokens.
00:02:08 Priya: yes some do — for example agent-assist we append last n messages, so the input prompt can jump by 300 tokens on long threads.

00:02:25 Samir: important for sizing — longer context increases KV cache usage and affects per-token latency. our runtime picks kernel paths differently for >2048 context lengths, so that boundary matters.
00:02:40 Marco: what's the tail we care about — for us product wants P99 end-to-end under 1.5s for the short flows, and under 3.5s for gen flows up to 1k tokens. for >1k tokens we'd accept slower but need to know cost.
00:02:55 Alex: fine to use that as initial success criteria. we'll design benchmarks to mirror your 75th/90th/99th cohorts and measure both latency and cost per 1k tokens.

00:03:10 Diane: on quality — how will we measure hallucination or regression? we have internal evaluation prompts.
00:03:16 Samir: for the pilot we'll run a quality baseline: run your eval set against the Redwood model (we can use their currently validated open model in our catalog) and compute agreement/fluence metrics. if you have labeled ground truth we'll map to pass/fail thresholds.
00:03:31 Priya: we do have ~2k labeled cases for the critical intents, i'll include that in the artifacts.

00:03:40 Alex: next, replay vs shadowing for benchmarks. we usually recommend a two-phase approach: 1) synthetic replay of sampled logs to validate throughput and tail behavior in a controlled manner, 2) shadowed live traffic for the highest-risk endpoints to validate correctness and network interactions. any constraints on sharing logs?
00:03:58 Priya: security is tight, so anything we share has to be anonymized — PII scrubbed. we can provide aggregated token histograms and replay with placeholders. we also require SOC2 and certain audit artifact checks — do you have that?
00:04:12 Alex: Redwood has SOC 2 and audit logs for Private and Dedicated; we'll attach the security pack. for Hosted we still have SOC 2 but customers often prefer Dedicated/Private for ingesting sensitive support transcripts.

00:04:27 Marco: VPC peering — if we do Dedicated or Private, what does the network flow look like? any long maintenance windows? also how do you handle KMS for keys?
00:04:36 Samir: for Redwood Private we can do customer-managed KMS/HSM and the control plane sits in your VPC, or for Dedicated we offer per-tenant isolation with customer VPC peering. we'll share the network diagram. maintenance windows are negotiated, we support rolling upgrades and have SLA for uptime.
00:04:52 Priya: good. timeline — we'd like a 4 week pilot: week 0 onboarding & log handoff, week 1 replay benchmarks, week 2 shadow test on a single endpoint, week 3 analysis and tuning. possible to start by 2026-07-20?
00:05:06 Alex: yeah that's plausible if we get the artifacts. we'll need sample logs and tests by 7/14 ideally.

00:05:12 Diane: cost targets — we'd like <$0.60 per 1k output tokens on average across gen flows, is that realistic?
00:05:19 Samir: depends on model family and quantization; with batching and prefix caching we can get close on 8-bit quantized variants but quality tradeoffs apply. we'll run cost sims in the worksheet.
00:05:30 Priya: there's also token drift — we saw last quarter that our average output tokens crept up ~12% month-over-month. curious how you handle re-benchmarking for drift?
00:05:40 Alex: we recommend periodic replays and set up monitoring: token histogram retention, regression alerts on eval prompts, and automatic suggestions for different quantization profiles. Redwood Optimize can surface when drift increases cost beyond thresholds.

00:05:58 Marco: on burst handling — our worst-case hit is an external batch restart that aligns with customer-facing peak and creates a 10x spike, lasts ~3 minutes. can you simulate that?
00:06:08 Samir: yes our synthetic driver can do burst windows and we record cold vs warm kernel paths. important to emulate the distribution: are the bursts uniformly larger requests or many small ones?
00:06:18 Priya: mostly many small ones for classification, but sometimes it's a mixed batch. we'll provide separate samples for classification vs conversation endpoints.

00:06:30 Jules: small note — for the classification flows we often recommend a specialized light model variant to keep cost down; we can include that as a fallback policy in the benchmark plan.
00:06:41 Diane: how much instrumentation do you need from our side? logs, tracing headers?
00:06:46 Samir: request logs with timestamps, request id, prompt token counts, response token counts, and whether the call used context snippets. traces are optional but helpful for debugging P99 spikes. a simple CSV is fine.

00:06:59 Priya: ok we'll pull the last 14 days and scrub PII, should be able to produce the CSV.

00:07:05 Alex: i'll outline the benchmark worksheet: sample selection rules, replay driver config (qps ramp, steady-state, burst windows), metrics captured (P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost estimate), and quality checks (accuracy on labeled set).
00:07:22 Priya: do you support measuring prefix cache hit rates? we want to know if similar promp- — similar contexts are cached — you'll be able to measure that?
00:07:30 Samir: yes, runtime reports prefix/KV cache hit ratios and we can instrument the replay to show cache warmup curves. that's where you get big wins on cost and tail reduction.

00:07:45 Marco: what about concurrency limits and throttling? if we hit a very large burst, will requests be queued or dropped? what's the degrade behavior?
00:07:54 Alex: we expose policies — queue with backpressure and adaptive shedding to preserve SLOs for critical endpoints, and fallback to smaller model variants if defined. we'll document recommended thresholds for each endpoint.

00:08:08 Diane: for pilot acceptance, i'm listing pass criteria: 1) P99 within target for 75% of endpoints, 2) cost <= target for 80% of traffic by token-weighted average, 3) no regression above X% on labeled eval set.
00:08:22 Alex: sounds reasonable. we'll also add operational check: SRE runbook and run-the-book handoff.

00:08:28 Priya: one more question on streaming — we do partial streaming for responses, do you measure per-token latency in streaming mode?
00:08:35 Samir: yes we measure token emission rate and first-byte latency; streaming changes the tail characteristics slightly, we'll include both streaming and non-streaming scenarios.

00:08:48 Priya: ok great. can you give a rough back-of-envelope on GPU sizing for our peaks?
00:08:53 Samir: with your mix — classification-heavy short requests and long gen tails — initial estimate: baseline 18 QPS with average 180 tokens maps to roughly 0.6 effective GPU units under continuous batching assumptions; peak concurrency ~260 with mixed token sizes suggests we'd need elastic headroom approx 6-8x baseline or a Dedicated pool sized to handle concurrency spikes, or autoscale on Dedicated with burst buckets. we'll formalize numbers in the worksheet.
00:09:17 Alex: another point — for >2k token flows we may want to use a compilation path that is slower but memory efficient; that affects cost. we'll document recommended model variants.

00:09:28 Priya: timeline recap? artifacts & logs by 7/14, worksheet and replay config from redwood by 7/12, kickoff week of 7/20?
00:09:36 Alex: yes. we'll aim to start replay the week of 7/20 and have an initial report end of week 1 of the pilot.

00:09:42 Diane: anything else around compliance? we need audit logs retention details for 12 months, and ability to revoke keys.
00:09:50 Samir: we'll include the retention matrix and KMS revocation procedures in the security pack.

00:09:58 Priya: ok i'm comfortable. one last thing — data residency, some EU traffic must stay in eu-west-1 region. is region pinning available?
00:10:06 Alex: yes region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. for Hosted we can route to regionally located endpoints; we'll put the options in the doc.

00:10:18 Alex: great, i think that's it for the major points. we'll capture action items and send an email with the plan. thanks everyone.

[conversation continues with clarifying Qs and short exchanges, timestamps elided for brevity]

00:45:12 Priya: one micro detail — do you collect per-request cost attribution so we can map to product lines?
00:45:21 Samir: yes, Console can do token-level cost attribution and per-route dashboards, we can show token spend by service.
00:45:30 Marco: for the replay driver, can we throttle the egress to match our peering limits?
00:45:36 Jules: yes, the driver supports network shaping and QPS caps.

00:52:05 Diane: recap and owners?
00:52:09 Alex: Alex send worksheet (7/12), Priya provide logs (7/14), Samir sizing and infra options (7/15), Marco confirm egress policy (7/16).
00:52:20 Priya: sounds good.
00:52:24 Alex: ok we'll close. thanks everyone.
